_note: Where things stand, as data (MIGRATION_3D §6.2, M1a). A position is an ANCHOR: a place or a named point plus an offset in tiles, or a feature — a prop of that kind standing in the place — plus an offset. Content names what it stands next to and never a coordinate, so when the map moves under it, it moves with the map. The eight places' centres and footprints are here too; core/region.gd reads them and carries no site of its own. Offsets are [dx, dy] with y down. The bake (M1b) will write the places and points from the 3D workshop's data; everything below them is ours and stays.
_order: campfires are listed in the order they are searched: a place's own fire first, then the fairies', then the road's.
_bram_post: O14, 2026-09-29: where Bram stands and calls from, and brindle_hail and brindle_hail_east the two halves of the ground he watches — the village's edge on the side the graves are, where the road from them comes in (content/hail.json holds their radius). Named points on each world rather than Brindle plus an offset, because Brindle is 35x30 on his map and 15x11 here and one offset cannot mean the same street on both. On the baked world the brief writes both; these rows are the 2D map's.
_hails: Who calls out to a player walking into their ground, and from which point: {who, point, radius}. Filled on 2026-09-29 (O17), the day the hail could be seen. An empty list holds nobody, ever, which is the one-change way to take it out again.

hails._why: O17, 2026-09-29: the tutorial's way in (Yannick's « dresseur Pokémon »). Walk up from the graves into the village's edge and Bram, at his post up the trail, sees you, calls, and comes over. Once: hailed:bram, and never to somebody who has met him or killed him. Emptying this list takes it out again, whole.

the other half of his ground: two discs side by side make the barrier across the village's south edge (content/hail.json). The first row that sees you calls; the second never calls twice, because the fact is his, not the row's.

_cinderworks_gate: the works' yard gate (G3, 2026-09-21). On the baked world the bake writes this point at the passage of his portail_cour and this row is overlaid; on the 2D map it is the road in front of the tile the old guard stood on, which is a wall there (moved a row south on 2026-09-29, when the anchors began to be checked before they are nudged), so the gatekeeper resolves on both worlds.
_wild_note: WHERE THE WOOD IS DANGEROUS (W2, 2026-09-25). A pack is an anchor and a count, and it stands where it stands until somebody walks into it. NOTHING HERE CLOSES A ROAD: a player who wants one of these fights it or goes round, and the demo's funnel is made of where the wolves are rather than of any check in core/ (PLAYER_MODEL.md section 8, invariant 4). Taking the funnel out again is W4, and it is editing this list. Anchors were checked against the baked world rather than guessed: road_last_stop was tried first and dropped because it resolves INSIDE Cairnwell, and monsters never stand in a town.

wild._why: BEFORE THE BRIDGE, in the middle of the drawn road three tiles short of the deck — on the road and not beside it, because a player follows the road his brother drew and a pack in the grass next to it is walked past (Yannick, 2026-09-26: des loups avant le pont pour l'aciérie). They guard the crossing from the Brindle side, so the river is the thing the fight is fought for. It was first a third of the way out of Brindle, which is the way out to everywhere and six journey tests walked into it; then two thirds, which put it just past the far end of the bridge. TWO, because this is the first real fight after the tutorial and it must be survivable by somebody who has just learnt which key strikes
The climb, 126 tiles off the demo's road. Three: this is a road the demo does not want a first-time player on, and the difference has to be felt rather than announced.
The junction toward the Muster, 86 tiles off the demo's road. Same reason, same count. Pillar 1 is untouched: the road is open and Blackcairn is reachable in minute one, at a price.

bram._why: 2026-09-19 (F2): the first person the player can fight. Since O14 (2026-09-29) he stands at a point of his own on each world — the same tile Brindle+(2,-4) gave him, which was picked by asking BOTH worlds for a prop-free tile: (3, 2) put him behind one of his brother’s trees on the baked map and was not clear on the procedural one at all.

sena._why: 2026-09-19 (Q1/Q2, then playing it): she stood at +4,+1, which is where the yard fence now runs — inside her own workplace’s wall. Moved to -7,+5 by eye, and Yannick played it and could not find her: she was standing under his roofs, invisible. Chosen the way Bram’s was now, by asking BOTH worlds for a tile with nothing within two of it, and still by the common kitchen, which is where Tom says to look.

tom._why: 2026-09-19 (Q2): by the cart sheds, the far side of the quarter from Sena, so that finding one is not finding both. Sena tells the player where he is.

strangers._why: 2026-09-15: stand on the delivered diagonal deck, not beside its parapet

2026-09-21 (G3): the man in the passage of his portail_cour, with lines of his own rather than the bridge guard's. Anchored on the gate's point, so wherever the brief puts the gate he stands in it. The passage is open ground with somebody standing in it — see WardRules — and choosing a side is what gets you past him (Q3).
a row further from the kiln than he stood until 2026-09-29: (2, 3) was a wall on the 2D map

the workers', downwind of the kilns. Three tiles west since 2026-09-29: (-9, 9) was in the river on the 2D map
the inn yard, outside the gate
the tenants', at the field's edge
a picket fire, outside the camp proper
the quay, where the boats tie up
the carters' yard outside the walls
the last verge before the gate. A row south since 2026-09-29: (8, 9) stood on his ramparts
the fairies' fire, among the graves since O12: the first save in the game. Two tiles off on both axes, beyond the fire's reach of the wake tile, so the first key hears her before it rests you
short of the bridge, on the Brindle side
the long empty stretch west of the river
the Muster junction, outside the camp
Kell's, deep in the Thornwood: a deserter hiding in a wood has a fire, and it is the only landmark out there
the ferryman's, on the Saltmarch spur where the marsh begins

the one stall nobody watches (§8): off the trunk road, on the north edge, verified against a roused watch
